record_body:
Account summary
- Regulated fintech prospect evaluating Redwood for LLM features in advisor workflows + internal ops.
- Strong interest in Redwood Private (VPC) for any workload that touches customer data. Hosted API is OK only for non-sensitive experimentation.
- They came in through lifecycle retargeting (LinkedIn) and asked pointed questions about compliance claims + data handling. Needs careful messaging: avoid implying “out-of-the-box” compliance certifications beyond what we can substantiate.

Primary contacts (as captured on calls/emails)
- Director of Platform Engineering (technical buyer)
- Security GRC Manager (blocks/approves vendor)
- Product Manager, Advisor Experience (use-case owner)

Use case / workload
- Summarization: meeting notes + call transcripts for advisors (PII/financial data likely present).
- Internal knowledge search: policy/procedure retrieval for ops (mix of confidential + public docs).
- Support-agent (internal): triage of advisor support tickets.
- Expected traffic: initial pilot 5–10 req/s, then scale to 50–100 req/s in peak windows if rolled out.
- Latency target: <1.5s time-to-first-token for chat flows; streaming required.

Product fit notes
- Wants: Private deployment (VPC), audit logging, KMS integration, clear retention controls, and region pinning.
- Dedicated capacity is a potential interim option if we can guarantee data isolation + strict log retention, but they prefer VPC.

Security / compliance questions (verbatim-ish)
- “Do you store prompts/responses by default? If so, where, and for how long?”
- “Can we disable all content logging and still get basic metrics?”
- “How do you handle UTM parameters and attribution—do those end up in event logs tied to a user?”
- “Is SSO/SAML available for the console? Any SCIM?”
- “Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM?”
- “Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS) and key rotation?”
- Data residency: US-only requirement for pilot. (They asked for a written statement they can put in the vendor packet.)

Lifecycle / growth experiments sensitivity
- Flag for Marketing/Growth: QuartzFin is particularly sensitive to marketing language and “implied guarantees.”
- Do not send claims like “SOC2 compliant in days” / “instant compliance” / “air-gapped on request.”
- They reacted negatively to generic onboarding messaging that points to Hosted API quickstart without clear data-handling caveats.
- Requested: an “enterprise onboarding path” that leads with VPC/private options and a short compliance FAQ. Also asked to be excluded from automated sequences once sales-engaged.

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-01-22: Inbound via retargeting ad + landing page; filled form requesting Private/VPC info.
- 2026-01-24: Intro call (Avery Johnson + Aparna Reddy). High-level architecture discussion; they asked for security documentation early.
- 2026-02-03: Follow-up email from QuartzFin security: retention, telemetry payload examples, and where attribution parameters are stored.
- 2026-02-11: Internal note: coordinate with Growth team to suppress from self-serve onboarding email sequence once opportunity is created.
- 2026-02-21: Call w/ Security GRC + Platform Eng. They are open to a limited POC if we can confirm: (1) VPC deployment scope/timeline, (2) data retention defaults + ability to turn off content logging, (3) SSO for console, (4) audit log export.

Open questions / to validate
- Whether they require on-prem or just VPC (they said “VPC is fine for now, on-prem is a longer-term question”).
- Whether they need specific compliance frameworks beyond SOC2 (they hinted at ISO + customer due diligence).
- Whether their model preference is fixed (they asked about open models and ability to pin versions for change control).

Internal handoff notes
- Sales/CS: Treat as compliance-first deal; push to a formal security review before any self-serve activation nudges.
- Marketing Ops: Ensure suppression rules work (no additional onboarding emails once sales-engaged). Avoid aggressive retargeting frequency.
- Product/Growth: This account is an example of why lifecycle experiments must avoid over-promising and must have clear enterprise paths (VPC/private messaging, retention/residency callouts).
